ci.inertReason: Which changed paths are allowed to shrink a CI run. This list is an ALLOW-LIST and the default is the full suite: a changed path matching nothing here forces `verify-browser` + `verify-integration` to run and every `verify:self` lane to run. That direction is the whole safety property — a new package, a new top-level directory, or a file nobody classified is covered by default, and no catch-all rule has to be remembered. Adding an entry is the only way to make anything skippable, which is why this file is code-owned (.github/CODEOWNERS) and why touching it lands in `ciConfig` below and forces a full run on its own PR. Never invert this into a list of paths that DO trigger things.

inert.reason: The agent-pipeline copy. Safe to isolate for two independent reasons: knip.json ignores `scripts/**` entirely, so it cannot affect the dead-code gate, and nothing under packages/ imports it (it is a standalone npm package outside the pnpm workspace, which is why `verify:fast` never reaches it). The `pipeline-drift` job stays ungated and still checks this directory against the pinned wafflebase/agent-pipeline commit.

Prose. Maps to the entropy lane rather than to nothing because entropy.docStaleness.designDir below is `docs/design`, so a design-doc edit genuinely can fail that gate. Root-level `*.md` only — the single `*` does not cross a separator, so packages/README.md is deliberately NOT matched and falls through to a full run.
Agent-facing instructions. Read by Claude Code, executed by no lane. Empty tags means a .claude-only PR runs no verify:self lane at all.

The VitePress docs site. A workspace package, but a leaf one: nothing imports @wafflebase/documentation, so it cannot reach the engines, the frontend, or the browser/integration jobs. It is called out explicitly because it is the one packages/ entry that is genuinely inert, and because publish-ghpage.yml builds it at deploy time — the `documentation:build` lane exists so a broken docs build fails CI rather than the deploy.

ci.ciConfigReason: The gating surface itself. A change to any of these forces a full run, so a PR can never use the filter to grade its own homework — the reduced-run decision is always made by the version of the mapping already on main. It also drives the loud `ci-config-changed` label and job-summary warning, because CODEOWNERS only binds when branch protection has 'Require review from Code Owners' switched on.

chunkBudgets.maxChunkCountReason: Bumped from 147 → 215 for Mermaid diagrams in the Notes markdown preview (issue #625). This is a large, deliberate bump: `mermaid` splits itself per diagram type (36 `import()`s of `dist/chunks/mermaid.core/*Diagram*.mjs` plus their shared cytoscape / d3 / dagre / katex deps), so wiring it in through the single `import('mermaid')` in `packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts` adds a measured 66 deferred chunks (144 → 210 measured on the rebased tree, cap set to 215 for headroom). Keeping upstream's own splitting is the point: a note with a `flowchart` fence downloads `mermaid.core` (~618 kB) plus that one diagram module, not the whole ~2.5 MB engine — folding it all into one `manualChunks` vendor chunk would triple the bytes for the common case and risks coupling the shared deps (katex is already in `notes-view`, d3 in recharts) into an eagerly-loaded chunk. Nothing is downloaded on a note without a mermaid fence: `notes-view-*.js` measured 1298.92 kB → 1302.82 kB (+3.90 kB, just the placeholder/render pass), and no other route reaches the mermaid graph. Largest new chunk is 691 kB (`cynefin-*`), under the unchanged 710 kB global per-chunk cap, so no KB override was needed. The sanitizer that guards the rendered SVG (`dompurify`, ~20 kB) is loaded next to the engine rather than statically, so it stays off `notes-view-*.js` and costs at most one further deferred chunk — mermaid already depends on it, so it is bytes a diagram was paying for anyway. The 5 chunks of headroom above the measured 210 absorb it. Prior bump: 145 → 147 for hoisting the upload panel into the app shell. The upload queue is an app-scoped module singleton, but its panel was rendered only inside `document-list.tsx`, so navigating to Data Sources / Analytics / Settings unmounted it and a still-running background import (a Miro board can run for a minute) vanished from view. Moving `<UploadPanel />` into `app/Layout.tsx` — the shared shell those routes all render inside — makes Layout a SECOND separately-split importer of the panel and its `upload-queue` store, so Vite hoists them out of the document-list route chunk into their own shared chunks (`upload-queue-*.js` and the panel), the same second-importer hoist pattern as the other shared primitives. Deliberately not mounted at the router root: the editor routes live outside Layout and the board minimap already owns that bottom-right corner. Only the workspace shell routes pull these in; the per-chunk KB cap is unchanged. Prior bump: 144 → 145 for the Miro board import (board SP3). `apply-imported-content.ts` now imports `YorkieBoardStore` to persist a mapped Miro board headlessly, which makes it a SECOND importer of that module alongside `board-view.tsx` — so Vite hoists the store out of the board-view route chunk into its own shared `yorkie-board-store-*.js` chunk, the same second-importer hoist pattern as the other shared primitives. The Miro import dialog, its summary formatter, and the `@wafflebase/board` Miro mapper all fold into the existing `document-list` chunk (no new route), and the backend proxy adds no frontend code at all. Only the documents-list and board routes pull the hoisted store in; the per-chunk KB cap is unchanged.
